_about: Demo L (enterprise risk walk-through). Single source for the static HTML in m11.html (written by scripts/invisible_engine/content/inserts.py) and for enterprise.js; tested by invisible-engine/tests/demos.mjs. Every recommendation names who can actually implement it. Tags locate assets, never people; nothing here recommends watching employees.

scenarios.label: A visitor’s phone alerts
scenarios.situation: A visitor’s phone says an unknown tracker seems to be moving with them while they are in your building.
scenarios.limit: The visitor’s phone, account and belongings are theirs. The company can offer help; it has no authority over them.

controls.do: Offer a private place, a calm contact and time; let the visitor decide what happens next.
If they ask, help them use their own phone’s tools to look for the item; remind them that disabling a tracker can alert whoever placed it.
controls.who: Security staff, at the visitor’s request

controls.do: Publish a visitor notice that says how to report a tracker alert and who will help.
Keep an escalation path to local police and support services for the visitor to use if they choose.

scenarios.label: An employee reports an alert
scenarios.situation: An employee reports an unknown-tracker alert and is worried about who placed it.
scenarios.limit: The employee’s personal phone and accounts are theirs; the company helps on request and never takes over.

controls.do: Respond confidentially and without blame; put the person’s safety first, before anyone disables anything.
Follow a documented process with due process for anyone accused, and privacy and legal review before any investigation.
On request, help review sharing and trusted devices on company accounts and devices (for example with Safety Check on a company phone).
Where appropriate, route requests for the paired account through law enforcement and the vendor’s published process.

scenarios.label: An executive travels
scenarios.situation: An executive travels to a public conference and wants to keep their movements private.
scenarios.limit: Precautions are offered, not imposed; personal devices stay personal.

controls.do: Give a short travel briefing: what an unknown-tracker alert looks like and whom to call.
Before the trip, review trusted devices and enable security keys or MFA on company accounts.
Agree a check-in plan and a contact who can arrange help discreetly.
Ask travel and event vendors how they handle attendee data and badges.

scenarios.label: Tags on company equipment
scenarios.situation: The company wants trackers on laptops and equipment cases to find lost assets.
scenarios.limit: Tags locate assets, never people. They go on company equipment only, never in personal items.

controls.do: Write a policy that tags locate assets, never people; tell staff where tags are and why.
Register company tags to company accounts, not personal ones, and remove them at offboarding.
Choose products with documented data handling and a data-processing agreement.
Tell staff that a company tag in a shared bag can trigger an unwanted-tracking alert, and how to report one.

safety: If anyone may be in danger, put their safety first: disabling a tracker can alert the person who placed it. Offer support; never require it.
